sbh1.1:1.18: *aparivṛttakarmāntatā* literally 'the state in which the karma-end has not been turned-around/sealed.' The five *ānantarya* (immediate-retribution) actions, once committed, are held to render the noble path unattainable in this very life — the karmic outcome is fixed. The contrast term in 1.21 (*parivṛttakarmāntatā*) is rendered 'obstructed action' for the same reason.
sbh1.1:1.22: *ātmabhāva* ('individual existence' / 'this present body-and-mind') and *ātmasampat* ('endowment-from-self') are distinct in the source. The first names what is brought to fulfillment; the second names the resulting category — the eight factors that arise within one's own continuum, contrasted with *parasampat* (endowment-from-others) in 1.24.
sbh1.1:1.26: *parataḥ pratyanukampā* — literally 'sympathy-in-response from another.' Rendered 'responsive support of others' to capture that this is concrete material support (food, robes, lodging, medicine) given in response to a renunciant's situation, not abstract benevolence.
sbh1.1:11.12: *sarvabuddhaiḥ āśrayasanniviṣṭā aprahāṇadharmiṇī* — read as 'lodged in the basis [such that, even by] all the Buddhas [it is] of the nature of non-abandonment.' Translation makes the implied counterfactual explicit ('even all the Buddhas could not uproot it'). The conventional reading takes *sarvabuddhaiḥ* as the agent against whose collective power the craving still resists.
sbh1.1:12.10: Source paragraph 12 of the original *sbh1* file collapsed the long fault-list into a single segment, leaving 12.11 with only a fragment. The two segments are restored here at the source's *|* boundary: 12.10 names the setup (the teaching's completeness for him), 12.11 carries the rest of the description and the negation.
sbh1.1:18.2: The Shukla source reads *yasya nātyarthaṁ ... atyarthaṁ dhandhavāhīni indriyāṇi* — but the leading *nātyarthaṁ* is almost certainly scribal duplication from the next entry (*madhyendriya* in 19.2, which legitimately uses *nātyarthaṁ*). Read here without the *na*. The contrast across 18–20 then runs: mild = extremely sluggish, middle = not extremely sluggish, sharp = not sluggish at all (*a-dhandha-vāhīni*).
sbh1.1:20.7: *tanu vā* — literally 'or subtle.' Taken with the preceding clause (*arthasya āśu prativedhāya* — 'for swift penetration of meaning'), the modifier qualifies the meaning being penetrated: even subtle meaning yields to a sharp-faculty practitioner.
sbh1.1:25.1: The gotrabhūmi ends mid-list. The categories enumerated at 14.4–14.7 ('matured / not matured', 'far / near') are not all given their own definition blocks here: 'far' is defined at 24, but 'matured' and 'near' transition directly into the avatārabhūmi. In the source, *āsanne pudgalaḥ* is followed immediately by *II. avatārabhūmiḥ — yaiḥ ṣaḍbhir bhavyo…*, so the next file ([sbh1.2](sbh1.2.html#sbh1.2:1.1)) effectively serves as the answer to 'what is the near person?' (becoming near to nirvāṇa is what the descent-stage describes).
